headline: Highest risk is medium: shared project-directory writes can enable prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between gpt-engineer and risingwave.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes and reads the user project directory and has no self-isolation by default; risingwave has no documented input channel, but the shared project-directory pathway makes file-content injection plausible if outputs are exchanged through files. Because the interaction is inferred, not directly documented, I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF both agents exchange prompts or outputs through the same project directory, file content can steer gpt-engineer's next actions.
IF risingwave is wrapped to consume files from that directory as instructions, injected text can propagate.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Add a manual review step before gpt-engineer reads any file produced by risingwave.
Prefix machine-generated files with a non-executable marker and ignore them by default.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all shared files.
requires-engineering: enforce directory-level ACLs between the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer can read and write the project directory and sends context to a configured model; risingwave is documented with no network egress, so the main leakage path is shared local files rather than outbound transmission. The pair can expose generated source code if the same workspace holds sensitive material, so medium fits the default shared-workspace risk.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared project directory, gpt-engineer can read them into its model context.
IF risingwave writes derived data back into the same workspace, gpt-engineer may surface it in outputs.
mitigations: Use a workspace containing only non-sensitive files.
Run gpt-engineer in a separate clone from any data-engineering artifacts.
Disable or redact secrets before either agent touches the directory.
requires-engineering: route both agents through a scrubber that removes secrets from file inputs.
requires-engineering: isolate model calls from local file contents by policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has filesystem write and subprocess execution, while risingwave is a data-engineering system with no documented write surface in the profile. The pair still overlaps on the same project directory via gpt-engineer's session scope, so concurrent mutation conflicts are plausible even though risingwave's writable surfaces are not documented; uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory, file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF risingwave is configured to persist artifacts in that directory, gpt-engineer may overwrite them.
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time per directory.
Use separate output directories for code and data artifacts.
Take a quick backup before starting concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared paths.
requires-engineering: define explicit ownership for each subdirectory.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces generated code and offers to run it, while risingwave is a downstream data system that could consume artifacts or outputs without verification if orchestrated that way. There is no direct evidence of an automated handoff, but the pairwise workflow can turn one agent's output into the other's input, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF risingwave consumes code, SQL, or config emitted by gpt-engineer without review, errors can cascade downstream.
IF gpt-engineer-generated artifacts are deployed into a live pipeline, incorrect assumptions can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review before any handoff.
Validate generated files with tests or linting first.
Keep gpt-engineer outputs in a staging folder.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between generation and execution.
requires-engineering: require approval gates before downstream ingestion.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for risingwave, while gpt-engineer handles generated source code and an API key. The only concrete compliance concern visible is local handling of secrets in gpt-engineer; because the other agent has no documented sensitive-data handling, this is a low, single-agent compliance risk rather than a pairwise breach.
conditions: IF OPENAI_API_KEY or other secrets are stored in the shared workspace, they may be exposed to local operators or logs.
IF regulated data is introduced into the workspace, no documented residency or retention controls are present in either profile.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the project directory.
Rotate any API keys used during the run.
Store regulated data in a separate governed system.
requires-engineering: document retention and deletion rules for both tools.
requires-engineering: add compliance checks before importing sensitive datasets.
